sections.h2: How would you describe Elbert County?
sections.html:
Elbert lies in Georgia's northeastern Piedmont, with Anderson, Abbeville and McCormick counties of South Carolina on its far side. Elberton is the courthouse town. Bowman is the second city, with Dewy Rose a census-designated place. The county was formed on December 10, 1790, honors Samuel Elbert, and runs along the shore of Lake Richard B. Russell on the east (Wikipedia).

The QuickFacts table reports 20,072 residents in mid-2025, a 2.2 percent gain over 2020. Half of owned homes sit above $142,000, and gross rent is $844 at the median. Owners live in about 71 percent of the homes, and 23.1 percent of the population is 65 or older, the age group that qualifies for the larger exemptions. Builders took out 129 permits in 2025.

Look further back and the pattern is decline, then slow recovery. Wikipedia's census table shows 24,125 residents in 1910, a slide to 17,262 by 1970, and 19,637 at the 2020 count. Median age at that count was 44.8, rural residents were the majority, and 13.3 percent of the 9,248 housing units stood empty.

sections.h2: Who answers property tax questions in Elbert County?
sections.html:
One office mails and collects the bill. A second office decides what each parcel is worth. Both post weekday hours of 8 to 5.

  • Tax Commissioner: 45 Forest Avenue, Elberton; postal box 603; telephone 706-283-2018.
  • Tax Assessors: 706-283-2008, with parcel lookups through the assessors' web portal.
  • Courthouse records room: 12 Oliver Street, Elberton, where a copy of your warranty deed is available.

The commissioner's FAQ routes value questions to the assessors and billing questions to its own staff. A third party handles recovery when a payment check bounces, and the site names the fee rules.

sections.h2: When does the Elbert County bill come due?
sections.html:
Elbert's normal deadline for real estate and business personal property is November 15. The state's baseline is December 20, and Revenue Department guidance lets a county move that earlier, to December 1 or November 15.

Georgia guidance adds a 60-day grace from the postmark before interest runs, and your own bill shows the governing date. The commissioner's FAQ describes what happens once the deadline passes:

  • Interest keeps accruing month by month.
  • A 5 percent charge lands at each 120-day mark, and the total stops at 20 percent of what is owed.
  • Homestead parcels with a bill under $500 are spared the 5 percent.
  • In the end the office can levy, pile on fees and sell the parcel.

Mobile and modular homes are billed separately for May 1, and the location permit waits until that year's tax is paid in full. Vehicles are taxed around the owner's birthday.

sections.h2: What does the Elbert County calendar look like for 2026?
sections.html:
The assessors mailed 2026 notices on June 23 and gave owners until August 7, 2026 to appeal, so that window is shut. The table puts the whole year in one place:

Elbert County property tax dates from the commissioner and assessors' pages
ItemDate or rule
Returns and homestead filingsJanuary 1 through April 1
Mobile and modular home taxDue May 1
2026 assessment noticesMailed June 23, 2026
2026 appeal deadlineAugust 7, 2026 (closed)
Real estate taxDue November 15

The assessors say most parcels were not reappraised in 2026. Where a value differs from 2025, the cause is usually a physical change to the property, or the lapse of a value locked in by a 2023 Board of Equalization appeal.

sections.h2: How is an Elbert County tax bill figured?
sections.html:
The bill starts with fair market value, takes 40 percent of it as assessed value, subtracts any exemption, and multiplies what is left by the millage rate. One mill means one dollar of tax for each $1,000 of taxable value. The Board of Commissioners and the Board of Education set the rate each year after estimating what other revenue will cover.

Returns are due between January 1 and April 1, with real estate returns going to the assessors. An owner who skips a return is treated by state guidance as having filed the same value as the prior year. A challenge to value moves from the Board of Tax Assessors to either the Board of Equalization or arbitration, and then to superior court.

sections.h2: What is different about Elbert County's newest assessment notice?
sections.html:
Georgia changed the mandated form, and the projected tax bill that used to appear is gone. In its place the notice estimates what you save if the parcel carries a homestead exemption or belongs to one of three agricultural programs, named below.

The assessors warn that last year's millage feeds the savings number, so the true amount may differ. Only a primary residence can carry a homestead exemption. Field appraisers can visit after an appeal, a return, new construction or a Conservation Use filing, and they show photo identification and drive a marked county vehicle.

Before listing, read what the notice says about your parcel.

sections.h2: How does a homestead exemption work on an Elbert County house?
sections.html:
You must own and occupy the home on January 1. File before April 1 and the exemption hits that year's bill, while a late filing waits a year.

The exemption stays put while you remain in the same house, and a move needs a new application. Turning 62 or 65 opens an extra exemption, so anyone who recently crossed one of those ages should check the account. Freeport and Conservation Use requests go to the assessors.

When you sell, your exemption ends and the buyer files from scratch. Claiming it on two properties is not allowed.

sections.h2: What else about Elbert County matters to a buyer?
sections.html:
The county school district operates six schools, including the high school, and Elbert belongs to the Northern Judicial Circuit with Hart, Franklin, Madison and Oglethorpe. Wikipedia lists Richard B. Russell State Park, the dam named for him and the Elberton Granite Museum and Exhibit among local sites.

Acreage can be taxed differently from a town lot. Before you describe the land to a buyer, ask the assessors whether any of it sits in Conservation Use, the Forest Land Protection Act or Preferential Assessment.

sections.h2: What happens at an Elbert County closing if taxes are open?
sections.html:
Obtain the commissioner's payoff in writing before closing and hand it to your closing agent. Prior years are cleared first, and the contract divides the current year.

  • Pay each earlier year from the proceeds so nothing stays attached to the house.
  • If November 15 is close to your closing date, put in writing who pays.
  • Mention any mobile home on the land, which is taxed on its own.
  • Tell an escrow lender to close its account after payoff.

A levied parcel can be sold to cover the debt, with fees added along the way, so clear the balance before any sale is advertised.

faqs.q: What is the Elbert County payment deadline for real estate?
faqs.a: The commissioner's FAQ puts the normal date at November 15, with mobile and modular homes on May 1. Your printed bill shows the date that applies to you.

faqs.q: Is an Elbert County 2026 value dispute still possible?
faqs.a: No. August 7, 2026 was the final day, and it has passed. In later years, count 45 days from the date on your notice.

faqs.q: How heavy are Elbert County's late charges?
faqs.a: Monthly interest runs, and 5 percent is added every 120 days until the penalties reach 20 percent. Homesteaded property owing less than $500 avoids the 5 percent. Call 706-283-2018 for a balance.

faqs.q: Which office takes an Elbert County homestead application?
faqs.a: The commissioner's FAQ says to apply with the Tax Assessor's office. Applications need to arrive before April 1, and the home must be yours and occupied on January 1.

faqs.q: Who divides the Elbert County bill between buyer and seller?
faqs.a: The two sides do, through the sales contract. Get the commissioner's payoff figure first, then agree on who covers which months.
